goals: Judge when stacking is worth the complexity
why: Stacking squeezes out the last bit of accuracy by combining different model types. It is common in competitions, rarer in production because of its complexity.
explain: Train several **diverse base models** (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, k-NN).
Use their predictions as features for a **meta-model** (often logistic or ridge regression) that learns **which model to trust when**.
The base-model predictions used for training the meta-model must be **out-of-fold** (made on data each base model did not see). Otherwise the meta-model learns from overfit predictions.
**Blending** is a simpler variant using one hold-out set. Gains are typically small (0.5–2%), so weigh them against maintenance cost.

example.title: Why a learned combination beats each model
steps: Six stores (monthly sales, ₹ lakh) with out-of-fold errors. Forest: +4, −2, +5, −6, +2, −3. Boosting: −3, +4, −3, +5, −4, +3. Linear: +8, −4, +7, −10, −6, +5
MAE: forest ≈ 3.67, boosting ≈ 3.67, linear ≈ 6.67. Simple average of all three: MAE ≈ 2.44
A meta-model with non-negative weights learns roughly 0.48 × forest + 0.52 × boosting + 0 × linear
example.result: Forest and boosting err in opposite directions, so the learned blend cancels most of their error and switches the weak linear model off. On six rows this is a demonstration; judge a real stack on a separate test set.

mistakes: Training the meta-model on in-sample predictions (leakage).
Stacking very similar models (no diversity, no gain).
takeaways: A meta-model combines diverse base models
use: Competitions, high-value predictions where every 0.1% matters
avoid: When latency, maintainability or explainability matter more

practice.code:
from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer
from sklearn.ensemble import StackingClassifier, RandomForestClassifier, HistGradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
X, y = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True)
st = StackingClassifier([("lr", make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))),
                         ("rf", RandomForestClassifier(200, random_state=0)),
                         ("gb", HistGradientBoostingClassifier(random_state=0))],
                        final_estimator=LogisticRegression(), cv=5)
print(cross_val_score(st, X, y, cv=5, scoring="roc_auc").mean().round(4))

check.q: Why must the meta-model be trained on out-of-fold predictions?
options: To avoid learning from overfit in-sample predictions

check.q: Stacking works best when base models are…

formula.plain: The final prediction is a constant plus each base model's (out-of-fold) prediction times a weight learned by the meta-model. A simple average is the case where every weight is 1/K.
